claims.text: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has superior molten-salt corrosion resistance compared with duplex stainless steel 2205 at 450 °C and 650 °C.
AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has superior tribo-corrosion resistance compared with duplex stainless steel 2205.
AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is a dual-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy.
The tested AlCoCrFeNi2.1 material is in an as-cast state.
AlCoCrFeNi2.1 contains a mixture of FCC and BCC/B2 phases.
The elements in the dual-phase AlCoCrFeNi2.1 microstructure are homogeneously distributed.
AlCoCrFeNi2.1 and DS2205 were evaluated in molten NaCl-KCl-MgCl2 at 450 °C and 650 °C.
The cited exposure included a tribological component such as sliding, rubbing, or applied contact load.
Molten-salt performance at these temperatures is relevant to concentrating solar-power and nuclear-energy applications.
The FCC phase acts as a protective barrier during exposure.
The B2 phase in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 undergoes selective dissolution in the molten salt.
Selective dissolution of the BCC/B2 phase induces micro-galvanic coupling and thereby mediates passivation.
Micro-galvanic coupling occurs between the two phases of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 and is associated with selective dissolution.
Exposure forms a surface layer enriched in noble elements originating from the FCC phase.
The work function of the exposed alloy surface increases.
The increased work function inhibits further oxidation.
Controlled selective dissolution of the BCC phase minimizes overall material loss.
AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has corrosion rates of approximately 1 mm/year at 450 °C and 9 mm/year at 650 °C.
DS2205 has corrosion rates of approximately 8 mm/year at 450 °C and 20 mm/year at 650 °C.
Processing variations, microstructural defects, and environmental fluctuations can materially change the corrosion rates and the contribution of micro-galvanic coupling.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis repeatedly frames the comparison as tribo-corrosion, but the described experiment is a molten-salt immersion corrosion study and specifies no sliding, wear, contact load, or other tribological action. Thus the proposed test cannot directly establish the claimed tribo-corrosion advantage.
